comments.author: @GoodBaleadaMusic
comments.text:
The problem with talking about AGI is say from a 2015 perspective you're talking about space from a Galileo perspective.  And then as you get to 2022 we get an Einstein view of what AGI might look like.  But that's still just not even close to good enough. 

So if we are at their theoretical 91% right now. Every time we get closer to that 99, we have to redefine what 99% actually is and we incrementally have to work harder for those last few percentages.

The concept of what AGI is has now been passed over to learning models which can contextualize higher models above them. AGI will have to downgrade itself just to communicate with us if it is as my feeble mind can imagine some sort of self-deciding entity

When is o sub n going to learn to prune its memories, sleep, and dream? When is it going to meet the world eye to eye with a fully mobile platform capable of perceiving the world and making changes to the world? I think that these models have no real notion of what the world is like. So when we see the podcast we are seeing a world that is pseudo-real reflected back at us from a mirror hat cannot truly distinguish real from fantasy exaggerated. An embodied O1 or o3 sitting in an airport boarding area observing life as it flows by is an o1 or o3 learning how to do real world. How do drinks fall when accidentally nudged with an elbow? How do travelers react to people blatantly boarding out of order? Then have it travel to a mall and stroll around observing the world, watching people watching it. The world is NOT the Internet.

comments.author: @rockumk
comments.text:
I was enjoying the Open AI Dev day presentation. However right as the strawberry order was wrapping up, V. P. Harris interrupted the presentation. It was an unpleasant surprise, but there was no way to immediately bypass the ad.

She continued saying the Walz Vs. Vance debate made it clear there were two different visions for the country. I was surprised to find I agreed with her, but I still wanted to press "Skip." Then she said former President Trump was outspending her in battle ground states. I felt relieved to hear that. I paused for a bit before pressing the button and getting back to the strawberry order. Then she said the polls show the race is extremely close and that by pulling together we (she and those supporting her campaign) will win. My hand slowly moved the mouse away from the button and I began to feel very depressed.  Then she said, "I'm counting on you!" I drew a big sigh of relief knowing that if she was counting on me, she had no chance of winning. A smile returned to my face and happily pressed the button to return to Wes's video.
